subject: Estimator selection in a MIMIC model

messages.author: 68876a04b840cbff
messages.subject: Estimator selection in a MIMIC model
parts:
Dear all,

I am running a MIMIC model in lavaan. The structure of the scripts is as following:

mimic <- fit.mimic = " F =~  X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 + X5 + X6;
                                 F ~  Y1 + Y2;
                                 X1 ~~ X3;
                                 X3 ~~ X5"
 
fit <- cfa (mimic, data, estimator = MLR)
or 
fit1 <- cfa(mimic, data, ordered = "X1", estimator = WLSMV)


in my data, X1 is binary, and my sample size is about 50. I tried both MLR and WLS (with set X1 as ordered, i.e. ordered = “ X1"), the results are really different. The MLR did not detect any significant relationships, while  WLS found many. I would like to ask which estimator I should use.

I read the book by Finch and French (Latent variable modelling in R, 2015), they mentioned if the data do not reach the assumption of multivariate normality, it is better to use WLS or its friends (WLSMV). And my data are not multivariate normal from Mardia test, as follow.

Mardia's Multivariate Normality Test 
--------------------------------------- 
   data : dataset 

   g1p            : 107.5234 
   chi.skew       : 1021.472 
   p.value.skew   : 1.128484e-06 

   g2p            : 301.5029 
   z.kurtosis     : 2.123852 
   p.value.kurt   : 0.03368251 

   chi.small.skew : 1081.817 
   p.value.small  : 1.032461e-09 

   Result          : Data are not multivariate normal. 

Also about residual covariances, I used MI to decide the inclusion and exclusion of the residual covariances. I found different set of residual covariances significantly affect the model fit. Is there any standard to keep the residual covariance, if the MI is bigger than 3.8, while we did expect the relationship between the variables ? 

Thank you a lot!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Estimator selection in a MIMIC model
parts: X1 is binary, and my sample size is about 50. I tried both MLR and WLS (with set X1 as ordered, i.e. ordered = “ X1"), the results are really different. The MLR did not detect any significant relationships, while  WLS found many. I would like to ask which estimator I should use.

MLR  adjusts test statistics and SEs for nonnormality, but still assumes the data are continuous with finite kurtosis.  Because X1 is binary, WLSMV sounds more appropriate.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Estimator selection in a MIMIC model
parts: in my project, X1 is an exogenous variable

No, it is endogenous.  It is an indicator of a latent variable, which means the latent variable explains/predicts X1.  But to answer your question, you do not need to declare an (actual) exogenous variable as categorical; rather, you need to create some kind of contrast code(s) to include them in the syntax (e.g., dummy codes, effects codes).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
